entries.title: verify gate 21 `leak-cjk` judges CJK-to-CJK jobs; `leak-scan` becomes SKIP and two gates disappear
entries.change: When source and output share the spaceless CJK family, the mapping's `lang` names a Han convention (ja / zh-Hans / zh-Hant), the source's convention can be read, and the pair is JP→SC, JP→TC, SC→JP, SC→TC or TC→SC, verify records a new gate `leak-cjk`. It FAILs when a drawn line holds 6 or more characters the target cannot carry, REVIEWs at 1–5, and PASSes otherwise, with one Finding(page, 'line', text) per line. In that case `leak-scan` is recorded as SKIP ('judged by leak-cjk') where it used to be REVIEW, and `leak-running` and `leak-isolated` are no longer recorded at all; v54 recorded them as PASS/PASS. So verify and run_verify can now return exit_code 1 on CJK-to-CJK jobs that used to be REVIEW only. When the tell cannot apply (no lang, a TC→JP pair, an unclear source), the old REVIEW leak-scan stays and the console gains the line `   (CJK tell not applied: <why>)`. GATE_NAMES gains 'leak-cjk' between 'leak-scan' and 'leak-running'.

entries.title: A merge's reported scale is source-relative, including the 0.98 fit allowance (shipped without a version bump)
entries.change: Merges are drawn at round(size*0.98, 1) and then scaled by the Story engine. The ratio recorded and compared against the 0.7 floor used to be the engine's factor alone. It is now that factor times the drawn/source ratio of the fit allowance (0.9778 for a 9 pt source). Every merge therefore appears in the scaled runs at about 0.98 even when the engine did not shrink it, and `verify --translations` REVIEWs scaled-runs for any job with a merge. Reading the code (consider_ratio; I did not run this case): a merge whose engine factor is just above 0.7 (below about 0.716 for a 9 pt source) now falls under SCALE_MIN and is refused as overflow unless allow_scale names it. The drawing is unchanged: DECISIONS measures 8.2069 pt both before and after. Version caveat: c09449d reads 56.0.0 and landed on main at d3db869 without a bump, but main had already been 56.0.0 at bacc436 without it. The first version number that guarantees it is 57.

entries.title: All output goes through `logging`: loud calls also reach the root logger, the package logger is left at INFO, and compare()/render_pages() stop printing
affects: logger 'pdf_translate' (NullHandler added at import in v57)
entries.change:

entries.title: Typed refusals: the PdfTranslateError family, `refusals` data, and retypeset's precedence
entries.change:
New base class PdfTranslateError(Exception). It carries message, console_line, exit_code (1 by default; 2 for WidgetTextError), refusals (a dict of lists with cores untruncated) and to_dict(): {'schema': 1, 'version', 'error', 'message', 'console_line', 'exit_code', 'refusals'} plus details(). WidgetTextError now subclasses it; in v54 it subclassed Exception directly. strip_text.WidgetTextError re-exports the same class.
run_retypeset on a legacy mapping raises in this order:
- Before drawing: untranslated segments or unauthored merges raise MappingError (refusals 'untranslated' [{page, core}] and 'unauthored_merges' [{page, first_line}]).
- An unmatched merge or a bad merge box raises MappingError (refusals 'merges').
- Unplaceable notices raise PlacementError (refusals 'notices' [{index, why}]).
- After drawing: any glyph miss raises GlyphError (page, char, and face = the role label such as 'regular', not a path). Otherwise overflow or a rotated-shaped run raises PlacementError (page, key, scale; scale is None when only rotated runs refused).
- The post-draw refusals always carry the keys untranslated, overflow [{page, scale, core}], glyph_misses [{page, role, char, codepoint, name, core}] and rotated_shaped [{page, core}].
The v58 code also had an unreachable MappingError branch between GlyphError and PlacementError; cb3a670 (v74) removed it.
run_prepare_font raises FontError with reason 'fstype', 'no-pyftsubset', 'no-raster', 'no-conjuncts' or 'wrong-han-convention'. The loud wrappers catch PdfTranslateError, print console_line and return exit_code.
entries.consumer_action: Catch PdfTranslateError, or the specific types, around run_*. Branch on the type, exc.refusals and exc.reason, never on console text. `except WidgetTextError` keeps working.

entries.title: run_retypeset gains progress, cancel, scale_report and resource_root; HTML resources resolve against the mapping's directory

New keywords:
- progress(done, total): total counts pages plus merge jobs.
- cancel(): checked at the top of each unit; when it returns true, the call returns RetypesetResult(cancelled=True, output=None) and nothing is saved.
- scale_report: None writes no report, a path writes the report there, and the default writes it beside out.
- resource_root: authored merge and notice HTML resolves its resources against this directory, which defaults to the mapping's directory instead of the process cwd.

entries.title: Widget text is keyed by the fully qualified field name (R-03)
entries.change:
Scaffold keys are now every /T up the /Parent chain, joined with dots, with one entry per full name; before, only the first widget of each partial /T got an entry. choice_exports keys by full name and gives a repeated widget the key '<name> (widget n)'. How strip resolves each widget_text key:
- A full name applies to that field only.
- A partial name, or its base without [n], applies only when it names exactly one field.
- A partial name that names several fields raises WidgetTextError listing the candidates' full names.
- Two keys for one field raise WidgetTextError.
- Distinct widgets that share a full name but differ in the source text being written raise WidgetTextError.
Only /Widget annotations take part. The rewritten_widget_text entries name full names. Captions and hide_buttons still use partial names.

entries.title: No 4 pt floor on legacy shrink-to-fit: small print is drawn at the size that fits, and the 0.7x gate sees that ratio
affects: PlacementError (new refusals for runs that used to pass)
entries.change: At all four legacy shrink sites (plain run, leader label, RTL leader label, override part) the fitted size is fs * room / width with no minimum (a room of 1 pt or less counts as 1 pt), never above the source size. Before, every shrink was lifted to max(4.0, ...). Consequences: (a) a source of 5.71 pt or less that needed shrinking drew past its room at 4 pt and reported the lifted ratio (a 5 pt run needing 0.54x reported 0.8x and passed); it now reports the true ratio and raises PlacementError (refusals['overflow']) below 0.7x unless listed in allow_scale; (b) a source under 4 pt was drawn larger than the source and left out of the scale report; it is now drawn smaller and appears in scaled/scale_report.json. Measured on v81: fitted_size(5, 100, 54) = 2.7 where the v63 formula gives 4.0; fitted_size(3, 100, 50) = 1.5 where v63 gives 4.0. Review: IRS 1040-ES 'CAUTION' (5.25 pt) moved from a reported 0.7619 (pass) to 0.6642 (refused). An override part with empty text and max_width <= 0 no longer raises ZeroDivisionError (review).
entries.consumer_action: Expect new PlacementError refusals on forms with small print whose translation is longer; add those cores to allow_scale if a sub-4 pt size is acceptable. Treat scale-report ratios for sub-4 pt runs as changed.
entries.bytes_detail: Only runs whose fitted size would have been lifted to 4.0 pt: they are now drawn smaller. Review: on 10 wild PDFs, 33 runs changed, all from exactly 4 pt to smaller; renders differ on 13 of 272 pages in 7 files; no run got larger. A normal-size page whose shrinks stay above 4 pt is sha256-identical.
evidence: measured: fitted_size calls on the 0d58202 tree

entries.title: A typography-1 source-content refusal names the occurrence that holds the offending text, not the page's first segment
entries.change: Before, the refusal attached the first segment on the issue's page whatever text was at fault (235 of 366 wild content issues named another line), or {} when the page had no segments (page None). Now inspect_content records where the first offending text starts (text-line matrix tracked through Td, TD, T*, TL, ' and "; a covered glyph's centre for occluded text), and retypeset names the smallest segment whose box, widened by 1 pt, contains it: occurrence_id, source_text and MappingError.core are that segment's. A whole-page issue (UserUnit, unreadable content) or text no segment holds now gives occurrence_id None, source_text None, core None and page set to the issue's page. The reason, detail and which issue refuses first are unchanged, and typography verify's findings are unchanged because the position is not part of an issue's identity. The d4b0c24 code crashed on a /CropBox of fewer than four numbers; 85eb0d7 (also 72.0.0, merged in the same PR b0ed899 before release) makes such a box leave the position unknown. Known limit: on a line with several occurrences the line-matrix start can name the wrong one (proposal, REQUESTS-from-product.md:988).
entries.consumer_action: If code keyed on the typography refusal's occurrence_id/source_text/core, expect different (correct) values, and None for whole-page constructs.

entries.title: prepare_font instances the job's subset: no side files next to the output, and the instanced subset's summary fields and GPOS encoding differ
affects: the prepared font's head/hhea/vhea/OS/2/GPOS bytes (when instance= is given)
entries.change: Before v78, every call wrote <out>.chars.txt next to the output, and a call with instance= also wrote <out>.instanced.ttf, which was a whole-face instance. From v78 both working files go to a tempfile.TemporaryDirectory('prepare_font-...') and nothing is left next to the output. With instance=, the variable face is first cut in memory to the job's characters (_variable_subset keeps every feature, name record, table, glyph names and .notdef), and that subset is instanced. entries.title: verify gate 22 'widget-text' (REVIEW only) and a new widget_text= parameter
entries.change: verify and run_verify take widget_text=None, which accepts a path or an already-loaded dict. Without it, verify reads the widget_text.json next to translations, if one exists. The new gate always runs, right after opt-export-parity, so GATE_NAMES grows from 27 to 28 names and every later gate moves one place. For each field, the gate compares the output's tooltip (/TU), dropdown display labels, and text /V and /DV with the original's, by full field name and by export value. An unchanged string that contains a letter is REVIEW: one Finding(None, <full field name>, 'tooltip: ...' / 'value: ...' / 'default: ...' / 'option EXPORT: ...'). Strings count as kept on purpose, and stay silent, when the mapping deletes the field's key, leaves the slot out, or gives a target equal to its source. A null target excuses nothing. The gate PASSes with a count when nothing is left, records nothing when no field carries lettered widget text, and never FAILs. If the mapping's keys cannot be resolved (WidgetTextError), the gate runs without the mapping and says why in its message. It does not raise.
